record.original_question: For recursive path ordering with multiset and lexicographic status, is the existential fragment of the first-order theory of ordering constraints decidable when the precedence on function symbols is partial rather than total?

evidence.quote: Is satisfiability of lpo or rpo ordering constraints decidable in case of non-total precedences?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite signature of function symbols, each with a fixed arity, and let $\mathcal{X}$ be a countably infinite set of variables. Let $T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$ denote the set of first-order terms built from $\Sigma$ and $\mathcal{X}$. A precedence is a strict partial order $>_\Sigma$ on $\Sigma$ (not required to be total). To each $f\in\Sigma$ assign a status $\tau(f)\in\{\mathrm{mul},\mathrm{lex}\}$. The recursive path ordering with status $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ induced by $(>_\Sigma,\tau)$ is the relation on $T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$ defined recursively by: $s=f(s_1,\dots,s_m) >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t$ iff
1. $t=g(t_1,\dots,t_n)$ with $f >_\Sigma g$ and $s >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t_j$ for every $j$; or
2. $s_i \ge_{\mathrm{rpo}} t$ for some $i$ (where $\ge_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ is $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ together with syntactic equality); or
3. $t=f(t_1,\dots,t_m)$, $s >_{\mathrm{rpo}} t_j$ for every $j$, and $(s_1,\dots,s_m)$ is greater than $(t_1,\dots,t_m)$ in the multiset (resp. lexicographic) extension of $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ when $\tau(f)=\mathrm{mul}$ (resp. $\mathrm{lex}$).

An RPO ordering constraint is a finite conjunction of atomic constraints of the forms $u>_{\mathrm{rpo}} v$ and $u=v$, with $u,v\in T(\Sigma,\mathcal{X})$. The existential fragment of the first-order theory of $>_{\mathrm{rpo}}$ consists of formulas $\exists \bar{x}\,\varphi(\bar{x})$ where $\varphi$ is a Boolean combination of such atoms; satisfiability asks whether there exists an assignment of the variables to ground terms in $T(\Sigma)$ making the formula true.

Question: Is the existential fragment of the first-order theory of the recursive path ordering with multiset and lexicographic status decidable when the precedence $>_\Sigma$ is allowed to be an arbitrary strict partial order rather than required to be total? Equivalently, is satisfiability of RPO ordering constraints decidable for non-total precedences? (The same question is posed for the lexicographic path ordering LPO, the special case where every symbol has lexicographic status.)
artifact.status_search_result: Existing decidability/NP-completeness results for satisfiability of RPO/LPO ordering constraints (e.g., Nieuwenhuis's "RPO constraint solving is in NP" and related work) address the case of total precedences. Available sources indicate that the corresponding question for partial (non-total) precedences has not been resolved in the literature, and indeed the full first-order theory of LPO with partial precedence on a unary signature is known to be undecidable, while the existential fragment with partial precedence appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: RPO Constraint Solving Is in NP
status_evidence.snippet: A nondeterministic polynomial-time procedure for satisfiability of RPO constraints over total precedences.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability/NP results are established for the total-precedence case, not the partial-precedence case.

status_evidence.title: The Theory of Total Unary RPO Is Decidable
status_evidence.snippet: Decidability of the first-order theory of RPO for unary signatures with total precedence; contrasted with undecidability for unary signatures with partial precedence.
status_evidence.claim: Partial-precedence settings are known to cause undecidability for the full theory; the existential case with partial precedence is not settled by these results.

status_evidence.title: Solved Forms for Path Ordering Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Studies constraint solving for path orderings, focusing primarily on total precedences.
status_evidence.claim: Standard constraint-solving techniques target total precedences, leaving the partial case open.
